lessons.title: Google Maps: getting from A to B faster

steps.title: Live traffic and ETA
steps.body: Google Maps tracks live traffic (orange/red roads = busy) and adjusts your route and arrival time accordingly — handy when you don't want to be late for a shift or meetup.

steps.title: Multiple stops in one route
steps.body:
1. Set a route as usual
  2. Tap the plus icon (⋮ or 'Add stop') next to the address field
  3. Add a stop, like a shop or a friend who's carpooling
  4. Drag the stops into the order you want

steps.title: Offline maps for a festival or trip
steps.body: Heading to a festival, campsite, or abroad with poor signal? Download the area offline in advance: tap your profile picture > Offline maps > 'Select your own map'. This way navigation still works without internet.

lessons.title: Scoring secondhand and selling: Marktplaats & Vinted

steps.title: A listing that stands out
steps.body: Selling clothes, furniture, or stuff (nice side income)? Sharp photos in daylight, an honest description of flaws, and a realistic price — check similar listings before you set one.

steps.title: Paying safely, even under time pressure
steps.body: When in doubt, use Marktplaats's secure payment or Vinted's built-in payment, instead of a direct bank transfer. Watch out for buyers/sellers who pressure you to respond fast, or who want to arrange things outside the platform — a classic scam pattern.

steps.title: Known tricks
steps.body:
• A 'proof of payment' followed by a request for you to front the shipping costs yourself
  • An offer too good to be true, followed by time pressure
  • A payment link that isn't on marktplaats.nl or vinted.com

Not sure? Never agree to requests outside the platform, and ask someone for a second opinion if in doubt.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Browse a category that interests you below and note the price differences between similar listings.

lessons.title: Room hunting: finding a room or studio safely

steps.title: Setting filters and turning on an alert
steps.body: Set filters for price, location, and type (room, studio, apartment) on sites like Kamernet or Funda Rentals. Turn on an email alert — popular rooms sometimes only stay listed for a few hours before someone else grabs them.

steps.title: The classic room scam
steps.body: A 'landlord abroad' asking you to transfer a deposit plus first month's rent before you've ever seen the room is almost always a scam. Always view it in person first (or via a trustworthy video call with the current residents) before sending any money.

steps.title: What to pay attention to
steps.body:
• Is the lease in your name, and does the deposit match what's legally allowed?
  • Who are the housemates, and is there a trial period?
  • What's included in the rent (gas, water, electricity, internet)?

lessons.title: Seeing through the TikTok & YouTube algorithm

steps.title: Why your 'for you' feed is what it is
steps.body: TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube show content based on an algorithm: what you like, how long you watch, and what you skip shapes what you see next. Great for finding content you enjoy, but it can also keep you in a 'bubble'.

steps.title: Cleaning up your watch history
steps.body: Notice your feed getting one-sided (or showing more of a type of video you don't actually want anymore)? Go to your account > History and delete items, or deliberately tap 'not interested' on a video now and then.

steps.title: Subscriptions and notifications, under control
steps.body: Subscribe to channels/accounts you genuinely find interesting. Turn on the bell for instant notifications, or leave it off if you'd rather choose when you watch — saves a lot of 'just checking real quick' moments.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Check your YouTube watch history below and delete a few items you no longer find relevant.

lessons.title: 9292: getting to school, work, or a night out

steps.title: Saving favorite routes
steps.body: Traveling the same route regularly (school, internship, work)? Save it as a favorite so you can pull it up with one tap instead of typing everything in again.

steps.title: Checking disruptions before you leave
steps.body: 9292 shows live delays and disruptions on the rail network. Check alternative routes before you leave if a disruption is reported — saves you standing around on an empty platform for nothing.

steps.title: Student transit passes and subscriptions
steps.body: Traveling a lot outside your student transit hours, or finished studying? Compare travel subscriptions on your carrier's website (NS, GVB, RET, HTM) against your average travel pattern — it can save you real money.

lessons.title: Instagram, TikTok & Snapchat: taking control of your privacy

steps.title: Who sees what you post?
steps.body: Go to Settings > Privacy on Instagram or TikTok and check who can see your posts, stories, and profile: everyone, only followers, or a select group. Consider a private account if you don't want strangers seeing everything.

steps.title: Not sharing your location automatically
steps.body: Many apps automatically attach your location to photos and stories. Turn this off in the settings (on Instagram, for example: Settings > Privacy > Location Services) — especially handy if you don't want people knowing exactly where you live or hang out.

steps.title: What future employers (and future-you) will see
steps.body: A public profile can be viewed by anyone — including an internship supervisor or recruiter googling your name. Check your own profile as a 'stranger' now and then by logging out and seeing what's visible, and consider whether old posts still fit how you want to be seen.
